name: Chapter 4: The d- and f-Block Elements
description: Transition metal trends, oxidation states, E° values, magnetism, colour, catalysis, K₂Cr₂O₇, KMnO₄, lanthanoids and actinoids

cards.term: Which groups form the d-block?
cards.definition: Groups 3–12; d orbitals progressively filled in four long periods

cards.text: Inner transition series: 4f = {{c1::Ce to Lu}} ({{c2::lanthanoids}}); 5f = {{c3::Th to Lr}} ({{c4::actinoids}}).

cards.term: IUPAC definition of transition metals?
cards.definition: Metals with an incomplete d subshell in the neutral atom or in their ions

cards.term: Why are Zn, Cd, Hg not regarded as transition metals?
cards.definition: Full d¹⁰ configuration in the ground state and in their common oxidation states

cards.term: Why are Zn, Cd, Hg still studied with transition metals?
cards.definition: They are the end members of the 3d, 4d and 5d series

cards.term: Origin of the name "transition"?
cards.definition: Their properties were transitional between s- and p-block elements

cards.term: Inner transition elements used for nuclear energy?
cards.definition: Th, Pa, U

cards.term: General outer configuration of d-block elements?
cards.definition: \( (n-1)d^{1-10} \, ns^{1-2} \); exception Pd: 4d¹⁰5s⁰

cards.term: Why are there many exceptions in d-block configurations?
cards.definition: Very small energy gap between (n−1)d and ns, and extra stability of half-filled and full sets

cards.term: Configurations of Cr and Cu?
cards.definition: Cr: 3d⁵4s¹ (not 3d⁴4s²); Cu: 3d¹⁰4s¹ (not 3d⁹4s²)

cards.term: 3d series configurations at a glance?
cards.definition: Table 4.1 (1st series)

cards.term: 4d, 5d and 6d series configurations?
cards.definition: Table 4.1 (2nd–4th series)

cards.term: General configuration of Zn, Cd, Hg, Cn?
Sc is a transition element but Zn is not. Why? (Example 4.1)
cards.definition: Sc has 3d¹ (incomplete); Zn has 3d¹⁰ in atom and ion

cards.term: Silver is 4d¹⁰5s¹. Why is it a transition element? (Intext 4.1)
cards.definition: In its +2 state (Ag²⁺, AgF₂) it has an incomplete 4d⁹ subshell

cards.term: Why are d orbitals so influential in chemistry?
cards.definition: They protrude to the periphery of the atom, so they feel and affect surroundings most

cards.term: Characteristic properties caused by partly filled d orbitals?
cards.definition: Variable oxidation states, coloured ions, complex formation, catalysis, paramagnetism

cards.term: Horizontal vs group similarities in d-block?
cards.definition: Greater similarity along a horizontal row than in non-transition elements; some group similarity too

cards.term: Typical physical properties of transition metals?
cards.definition: High tensile strength, ductility, malleability, high thermal and electrical conductivity, metallic lustre

cards.term: Which transition metals lack typical metallic structures?
cards.definition: Zn, Cd, Hg and Mn

cards.term: Lattice structures of transition metals?
cards.definition: bcc, hcp, ccp (X = typical metal structure)

cards.term: Why are melting points of transition metals high?
cards.definition: Many (n−1)d + ns electrons take part in metallic bonding

cards.term: Trend of melting points along a series?
cards.definition: Rise to a maximum at d⁵, then fall; anomalies at Mn and Tc

cards.term: Why is enthalpy of atomisation maximum in the middle of each series?
cards.definition: One unpaired electron per d orbital favours strong interatomic interaction

cards.term: Metals with very high ΔaH° tend to be…?
cards.definition: Noble in their reactions (ΔaH° affects E°)

cards.term: Why is metal–metal bonding more common in heavy transition metals?
cards.definition: 4d and 5d metals have greater ΔaH° than 3d metals

cards.term: Why do transition elements have high enthalpies of atomisation? (Example 4.2)
cards.definition: Many unpaired electrons give stronger interatomic bonding

cards.term: Why is ΔaH° of Zn the lowest (126 kJ/mol) in 3d? (Intext 4.2)
cards.definition: No unpaired d electrons: 3d¹⁰ does not take part in metallic bonding

cards.term: Trend of ionic radius (same charge) across a series?
cards.definition: Decreases gradually: each new d electron shields poorly as nuclear charge rises

cards.term: Radii of 3d vs 4d vs 5d series?
cards.definition: 4d > 3d, but 5d ≈ 4d

cards.term: What is lanthanoid contraction?
cards.definition: Regular decrease in radii from La to Lu as 4f is filled before 5d

cards.term: Cause of lanthanoid contraction?
cards.definition: Imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another (poorer than d shielding)

cards.term: Main consequence of lanthanoid contraction for 4d/5d?
cards.definition: Similar radii, e.g. Zr 160 pm, Hf 159 pm: very similar properties

cards.term: Trend in density from Ti to Cu, and why?
cards.definition: Increases: radius decreases while atomic mass increases

cards.term: Trend of ionisation enthalpy across a transition series?
cards.definition: Increases, but less steeply than across a period of non-transition elements

cards.term: Which electrons are lost first when d-block atoms ionise?
cards.definition: ns electrons before (n−1)d

cards.term: Why does IE rise only slightly across 3d?
cards.definition: 3d electrons shield the 4s electrons fairly well from the rising nuclear charge

cards.term: Breaks in the steady rise of 2nd and 3rd IE occur at?
cards.definition: Mn²⁺ (2nd IE of Mn) and Fe³⁺ (3rd IE of Fe): both form d⁵

cards.term: Three factors in ionisation enthalpy?
cards.definition: Attraction to nucleus, electron–electron repulsion, exchange energy

cards.term: What is exchange energy?
cards.definition: Stabilisation ∝ number of pairs of parallel spins in degenerate orbitals (Hund’s rule)

cards.term: Why is 2nd IE of Mn lower than that of Cr?
cards.definition: Cr⁺ is d⁵ (stable, losing it costs exchange energy); Mn⁺ is 3d⁵4s¹ and loses the 4s electron

cards.term: Why is 3rd IE of Fe lower than that of Mn?
cards.definition: Fe²⁺ (d⁶) → Fe³⁺ gives stable d⁵; Mn²⁺ (d⁵) would lose it

cards.term: Why are 2nd IE of Cr and Cu unusually high?
cards.definition: Cr⁺ and Cu⁺ have stable d⁵ and d¹⁰ configurations

cards.term: Why is 2nd IE of Zn low?
cards.definition: Removing the second 4s electron leaves stable d¹⁰

cards.term: Why are oxidation states above +2 hard for Cu, Ni, Zn?
cards.definition: Their third ionisation enthalpies are very high

cards.term: Values: ΔiH (I, II, III) and other data for 3d metals?
cards.definition: Table 4.2

cards.term: Which 3d elements show the most oxidation states? (Intext 4.3)
cards.definition: Mn: all from +2 to +7 (4s² 3d⁵: most electrons to lose or share)

cards.term: Why fewer oxidation states at the ends of the series?
cards.definition: Too few electrons (Sc, Ti) or too many d electrons, fewer orbitals to share (Cu, Zn)

cards.term: Maximum stable oxidation state up to Mn equals?
cards.definition: Sum of s + d electrons: TiO₂, VO₂⁺, CrO₄²⁻, MnO₄⁻

cards.term: Typical oxidation states after Mn?
cards.definition: Fe(II, III), Co(II, III), Ni(II), Cu(I, II), Zn(II)

cards.term: Transition vs p-block variability of oxidation states?
cards.definition: Transition: differ by one (V²⁺, V³⁺, V⁴⁺, V⁵⁺). Non-transition: usually by two.

cards.term: Heavier members in d-block groups favour which states?
cards.definition: Higher states (opposite of the p-block inert pair effect): Mo(VI), W(VI) more stable than Cr(VI)

cards.term: Consequence: Cr₂O₇²⁻ vs MoO₃ and WO₃ as oxidants?
cards.definition: Dichromate is a strong oxidant; MoO₃ and WO₃ are not

cards.term: When are low (zero) oxidation states found? Examples?
cards.definition: With ligands that are π-acceptors as well as σ-donors: Ni(CO)₄, Fe(CO)₅ (oxidation state 0)

cards.term: Transition element with no variable oxidation state? (Example 4.3)
cards.definition: Scandium (only +3)

cards.term: Why is E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) positive (+0.34 V)? (Intext 4.4)
cards.definition: High energy for Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq) (high ΔaH° + IE) is not balanced by its hydration enthalpy

cards.term: Consequence of E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) > 0?
cards.definition: Cu cannot liberate H₂ from acids; only oxidising acids (HNO₃, hot conc. H₂SO₄) attack it

cards.term: General trend of E°(M²⁺/M) across 3d, and cause?
cards.definition: Becomes less negative: sum of 1st and 2nd IE increases

cards.term: Which metals have E°(M²⁺/M) more negative than the trend, and why?
cards.definition: Mn (stable d⁵ Mn²⁺), Zn (stable d¹⁰ Zn²⁺), Ni (most negative ΔhydH°)

cards.term: Thermochemical data behind E° values?
cards.definition: ΔaH°, ΔiH°₁, ΔiH°₂, ΔhydH°

cards.term: Why is Cr²⁺ reducing but Mn³⁺ oxidising (both d⁴)? (Example 4.4)
cards.definition: Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives d³ (half-filled t₂g); Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives d⁵ (half-filled)

cards.term: Why is E°(M²⁺/M) irregular for V, Cr, Mn…? (Example 4.6)
cards.definition: Irregular IE (ΔiH₁ + ΔiH₂) and low sublimation enthalpies of Mn and V

cards.term: Why is E°(Sc³⁺/Sc²⁺) low?
cards.definition: Sc³⁺ has a noble gas configuration (very stable)

cards.term: Why is E°(Zn³⁺/Zn²⁺) highest?
cards.definition: It would remove an electron from stable d¹⁰ Zn²⁺

cards.term: Why is E°(Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺) high but E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) comparatively low?
cards.definition: Mn²⁺ is d⁵ (stable, resists oxidation); Fe³⁺ is d⁵ (stable, easy to form)

cards.term: Why is E°(Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺) much more positive than Cr or Fe? (Example 4.7)
cards.definition: Very large 3rd IE of Mn (d⁵ → d⁴); so Mn(III) is of little importance

cards.term: Why is E°(V³⁺/V²⁺) comparatively low?
cards.definition: V²⁺ is stable: half-filled t₂g (d³)

cards.term: Why are Mn²⁺ compounds more stable to oxidation than Fe²⁺? (Ex 4.2)
cards.definition: Mn²⁺ is already d⁵; Fe²⁺ (d⁶) gains stability by becoming Fe³⁺ (d⁵)

cards.term: Highest oxidation states in 3d halides?
cards.definition: TiX₄, VF₅, CrF₆; Mn(VII) only as MnO₃F

cards.term: Why does fluorine stabilise the highest oxidation states?
cards.definition: Higher lattice energy (CoF₃) or higher bond enthalpy of covalent compounds (VF₅, CrF₆)

cards.term: Beyond Mn, which metals form trihalides?
cards.definition: Only FeX₃ and CoF₃

cards.term: What happens to V(V) halides other than VF₅?
cards.definition: Hydrolyse to oxohalides VOX₃

cards.term: Why is CuI₂ unknown?
cards.definition: Cu²⁺ oxidises I⁻: 2Cu²⁺ + 4I⁻ → Cu₂I₂ + I₂

cards.term: Why is Cu⁺ unstable in water? (Intext 4.9)
cards.definition: It disproportionates (2Cu⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Cu): much more negative ΔhydH° of Cu²⁺ outweighs the 2nd IE

cards.term: Highest oxidation state in oxides equals?
cards.definition: The group number, reached in Sc₂O₃ to Mn₂O₇

cards.term: Higher oxide of iron than Fe₂O₃?
cards.definition: None; ferrate(VI) FeO₄²⁻ forms in alkali but decomposes to Fe₂O₃ + O₂

cards.term: Oxocations that stabilise high states?
cards.definition: VO₂⁺ (V), VO²⁺ (IV), TiO²⁺ (Ti IV)

cards.term: Oxygen or fluorine: which stabilises higher states? Evidence?
cards.definition: Oxygen: highest Mn fluoride is MnF₄, highest oxide Mn₂O₇

cards.term: Why is oxygen better than fluorine here?
cards.definition: O forms multiple bonds to metals

cards.term: Structure of Mn₂O₇?
cards.definition: Covalent; each Mn tetrahedral, with an Mn–O–Mn bridge

cards.term: Why is the highest oxidation state shown only in oxides or fluorides? (Intext 4.6)
cards.definition: O and F are small and highly electronegative; O also forms multiple bonds

cards.term: Why does oxidising power rise VO₂⁺ < Cr₂O₇²⁻ < MnO₄⁻? (Example 4.5)
cards.definition: Increasing stability of the lower species they are reduced to

cards.term: Which 3d metal is not oxidised by 1 M H⁺?
cards.definition: Copper

cards.term: Why are Ti and V passive to dilute non-oxidising acids?
cards.definition: The reaction is kinetically slow even though feasible

cards.term: Strongest oxidising agents among M³⁺ in water?
cards.definition: Mn³⁺ and Co³⁺

cards.term: Which M²⁺ ions are strong reducing agents?
cards.definition: Ti²⁺, V²⁺, Cr²⁺: liberate H₂ from dilute acid (2Cr²⁺ + 2H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + H₂)

cards.term: Stronger reducing agent: Cr²⁺ or Fe²⁺? (Intext 4.7)
cards.definition: Cr²⁺: E°(Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺) = −0.41 V vs +0.77 V for Fe; Cr³⁺ is d³ (stable)

cards.term: Diamagnetic vs paramagnetic vs ferromagnetic?
cards.definition: Dia: repelled. Para: attracted. Ferro: attracted very strongly (extreme paramagnetism).

cards.term: Origin of paramagnetism?
cards.definition: Unpaired electrons (spin + orbital angular momentum)

cards.term: Why only spin counts for 3d ions?
cards.definition: Orbital contribution is effectively quenched

cards.term: Spin-only formula?
cards.definition: \( \mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \) BM (n = unpaired electrons)

cards.term: Spin-only μ for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5?
Magnetic moment of divalent ion of Z = 25? (Example 4.8)
cards.definition: Mn²⁺, d⁵, n = 5: 5.92 BM

cards.term: Spin-only μ of M²⁺, Z = 27? (Intext 4.8)
cards.definition: Co²⁺, d⁷, n = 3: 3.87 BM

cards.term: Calculated and observed moments for 3d ions?
cards.definition: Table 4.7

cards.term: Correction: Table 4.7 lists "Tl²⁺" as 3d². Which ion?
cards.definition: Ti²⁺ (titanium); Tl is thallium, a p-block element

cards.term: Trick: unpaired electrons from μ = 4.90 BM?
cards.definition: Solve n(n+2) = 24 → n = 4

cards.term: Why are transition metal ions coloured?
cards.definition: d–d transition: an electron excited to a higher d orbital absorbs visible light; we see the complementary colour

cards.term: What decides the frequency absorbed?
cards.definition: The nature of the ligand

cards.term: Identify the ions (left to right).
cards.definition: V⁴⁺, V³⁺, Mn²⁺, Fe³⁺, Co²⁺, Ni²⁺, Cu²⁺

cards.term: Which aquated 3d ions are colourless, and why?
cards.definition: Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺ (d⁰), Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰): no d–d transition possible

cards.term: Why do transition metals form many complexes?
cards.definition: Small ion size, high ionic charge, available d orbitals

cards.term: Examples of complex ions (NCERT)?
cards.definition: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺, [PtCl₄]²⁻

cards.term: Why are transition metals good catalysts?
cards.definition: Multiple oxidation states and complex formation; surface bonding raises reactant concentration and weakens bonds

cards.text:
Catalysts: {{c1::V₂O₅}} in the Contact process
{{c2::finely divided Fe}} in Haber process
{{c3::Ni}} in catalytic hydrogenation.

cards.term: How does Fe³⁺ catalyse 2I⁻ + S₂O₈²⁻ → I₂ + 2SO₄²⁻?
cards.definition: 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂; then 2Fe²⁺ + S₂O₈²⁻ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2SO₄²⁻ (Fe cycles between states)

cards.term: Intuition: why does Fe³⁺ speed up I⁻ + S₂O₈²⁻?
cards.definition: Both reactants are anions that repel; Fe³⁺ lets each react separately with a cation instead

cards.term: What are interstitial compounds? Examples?
cards.definition: Small atoms (H, C, N) trapped in metal lattices; non-stoichiometric: TiC, Mn₄N, Fe₃H, VH₀.₅₆, TiH₁.₇

cards.text:
Interstitial compounds: {{c1::higher}} melting points than pure metals
very {{c2::hard}} (some borides near diamond)
retain {{c3::metallic conductivity}}
chemically {{c4::inert}}.

cards.term: Condition for alloy (solid solution) formation?
cards.definition: Metallic radii within about 15% of each other

cards.term: Metals used to make steels and stainless steel?
cards.definition: Cr, V, W, Mo, Mn

cards.term: Alloys of transition with non-transition metals?
cards.definition: Brass (Cu–Zn), bronze (Cu–Sn)

cards.term: What is disproportionation? Example (Example 4.9)?
cards.definition: One oxidation state converts into a higher and a lower one: 3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O

cards.term: Which 3d metals form ionic MO oxides?
cards.definition: All except Sc

cards.term: Effect of increasing oxidation number on oxides?
cards.definition: Ionic character decreases, acidic character increases

cards.term: Nature of Mn₂O₇? What acids from Mn₂O₇ and CrO₃?
cards.definition: Covalent green oil Mn₂O₇ → HMnO₄ CrO₃ → H₂CrO₄ and H₂Cr₂O₇

cards.term: Nature of V₂O₃, V₂O₄, V₂O₅?
cards.definition: Basic → less basic → amphoteric (V₂O₅ mainly acidic; gives VO₄³⁻ and VO₂⁺ salts)

cards.term: Nature of CrO and Cr₂O₃?
cards.definition: CrO basic; Cr₂O₃ amphoteric

cards.term: Uses of K₂Cr₂O₇?
cards.definition: Leather industry, oxidant for azo compounds, primary standard in volumetric analysis

cards.term: Ore of chromium and first step to dichromate?
cards.definition: Chromite FeCr₂O₄ fused with Na₂CO₃ (or K₂CO₃) in free air

cards.term: Why convert Na₂Cr₂O₇ to K₂Cr₂O₇?
cards.definition: K₂Cr₂O₇ is less soluble and crystallises out; a non-hygroscopic primary standard

cards.term: Chromate ⇌ dichromate: effect of pH? (Ex 4.14)
cards.definition: Acid: 2CrO₄²⁻ (yellow) + 2H⁺ → Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange). Raising pH (OH⁻) turns dichromate back to yellow chromate.

cards.term: Oxidation state of Cr in chromate and dichromate?
cards.definition: +6 in both

cards.term: Structures of CrO₄²⁻ and Cr₂O₇²⁻?
cards.definition: Chromate tetrahedral; dichromate = two tetrahedra sharing one corner, Cr–O–Cr 126°

cards.term: Dichromate half-reaction in acid and E°?
cards.definition: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O; 1.33 V

cards.term: Why is Na₂Cr₂O₇ used in organic chemistry?
cards.definition: Greater solubility in water

cards.text: Acidified dichromate oxidises I⁻ to {{c1::I₂}}, H₂S to {{c2::S}}, Sn²⁺ to {{c3::Sn⁴⁺}}, Fe²⁺ to {{c4::Fe³⁺}}.

cards.term: Ionic equation: dichromate + Fe²⁺ (acid)?
cards.definition: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O

cards.term: Preparation of KMnO₄ (lab fusion)?
cards.definition: Fuse MnO₂ with KOH and an oxidant (KNO₃ / air) → dark green K₂MnO₄; it disproportionates in neutral/acid solution

cards.term: Commercial preparation of KMnO₄?
cards.definition: Alkaline oxidative fusion of MnO₂ → manganate, then electrolytic oxidation in alkaline solution → permanganate

cards.term: Lab preparation from Mn²⁺?
cards.definition: Oxidise with peroxodisulphate: 2Mn²⁺ + 5S₂O₈²⁻ + 8H₂O → 2MnO₄⁻ + 10SO₄²⁻ + 16H⁺

cards.term: Physical properties of KMnO₄?
cards.definition: Dark purple (almost black) crystals, isostructural with KClO₄; solubility 6.4 g/100 g water at 293 K

cards.term: Effect of heating KMnO₄ (513 K)?
cards.definition: 2KMnO₄ → K₂MnO₄ + MnO₂ + O₂

cards.term: Shapes and magnetism of manganate and permanganate?
cards.definition: Both tetrahedral. Green MnO₄²⁻: paramagnetic (1 unpaired e⁻). Purple MnO₄⁻: diamagnetic.

cards.term: Identify: shape, ion and colour.
cards.definition: Tetrahedral manganate ion MnO₄²⁻, green

cards.term: Identify: shape, ion and colour.
cards.definition: Tetrahedral permanganate ion MnO₄⁻, purple

cards.term: π-bonding in MnO₄⁻?
cards.definition: Overlap of O p orbitals with Mn d orbitals

cards.term: Unusual physical properties of KMnO₄?
cards.definition: Intense colour and diamagnetism with weak temperature-dependent paramagnetism (explained by MO theory)

cards.term: Correction/insight: why is MnO₄⁻ intensely coloured though Mn(VII) is d⁰?
cards.definition: Not d–d: it is charge transfer (O → Mn electron transfer absorbs strongly)

cards.term: Why doesn’t KMnO₄ oxidise water though E° says it should?
cards.definition: Kinetically very slow unless Mn²⁺ is present or temperature is raised

cards.term: Acidic KMnO₄: n-factor and product?
cards.definition: Mn²⁺ (5 electrons)

cards.term: Neutral/faintly alkaline KMnO₄: product?
cards.definition: MnO₂ (3 electrons)

cards.term: Ionic equation: permanganate + Fe²⁺ (acid)?
cards.definition: 5Fe²⁺ + MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺

cards.term: Ionic equation: permanganate + oxalate (acid)?
cards.definition: 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 2MnO₄⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 8H₂O + 10CO₂

cards.term: Why aren’t permanganate titrations done in HCl?
cards.definition: HCl is oxidised to Cl₂, using up extra KMnO₄

cards.term: Uses of KMnO₄?
cards.definition: Analytical oxidant, preparative organic chemistry, bleaching wool/cotton/silk, decolourising oils

cards.term: Why is La included with lanthanoids (symbol Ln)?
cards.definition: La closely resembles them

cards.term: Lanthanoids vs actinoids: overall chemistry?
cards.definition: Lanthanoids: very similar, essentially one stable state (+3). Actinoids: many oxidation states and radioactive: more complex.

cards.term: General configuration of lanthanoid atoms and Ln³⁺?
cards.definition: Atoms: 6s² with variable 4f (and 5d). Ln³⁺: 4fⁿ (n = 1–14).

cards.term: Which lanthanoids have a 5d¹ electron in the atom?
cards.definition: La, Ce, Gd, Lu (Gd: 4f⁷5d¹6s², Lu: 4f¹⁴5d¹6s²)

cards.term: Is the decrease in radii smoother for atoms or Ln³⁺ ions?
cards.definition: Ln³⁺ ions (regular); atomic radii are less regular

cards.term: Why are Zr and Hf found together and hard to separate?
cards.definition: Lanthanoid contraction gives almost identical radii (160 vs 159 pm)

cards.term: Most common oxidation state of lanthanoids?
cards.definition: +3

cards.term: Correction: NCERT says "La(II) and Ln(III) compounds are predominant." Right?
cards.definition: La(III) and Ln(III): La shows only +3; "II" is a typo

cards.term: Why do some lanthanoids show +2 or +4?
cards.definition: Extra stability of empty, half-filled or filled f subshell

cards.term: Ce(IV): why formed, and why a useful reagent?
cards.definition: Noble gas configuration (4f⁰); E°(Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺) = +1.74 V could oxidise water but reacts slowly: good analytical oxidant

cards.term: Lanthanoid well known for +4? (Example 4.10)
cards.definition: Cerium (Z = 58)

cards.term: Which lanthanoids show +4 only in oxides (MO₂)?
cards.definition: Pr, Nd, Tb, Dy

cards.term: Eu²⁺ and Yb²⁺: configurations and behaviour?
cards.definition: Eu²⁺ f⁷, Yb²⁺ f¹⁴: both reducing agents (revert to +3)

cards.term: Tb(IV): configuration and behaviour?
cards.definition: Half-filled f⁷; an oxidant

cards.term: Which lanthanoid behaves like Eu (both +2 and +3)?
cards.definition: Samarium

cards.term: Physical nature of lanthanoids?
cards.definition: Silvery white soft metals tarnish rapidly in air hardness rises with Z (Sm steel-hard)

cards.term: Melting range of lanthanoids? Exception?
cards.definition: 1000–1200 K; Sm melts at 1623 K

cards.term: Which lanthanoids break smooth density trends?
cards.definition: Eu and Yb (sometimes Sm and Tm)

cards.term: Why are Ln³⁺ ions coloured? Which are colourless?
cards.definition: f electrons (f–f transitions, narrow bands). La³⁺ and Lu³⁺ colourless.

cards.term: Which lanthanoid ions are diamagnetic?
cards.definition: f⁰ (La³⁺, Ce⁴⁺) and f¹⁴ (Yb²⁺, Lu³⁺); the rest paramagnetic

cards.term: First and second IE of lanthanoids?
cards.definition: ~600 and ~1200 kJ/mol (comparable with calcium)

cards.term: Lanthanoids with abnormally low 3rd IE?
cards.definition: La, Gd, Lu (f⁰, f⁷, f¹⁴ after ionisation)

cards.term: Chemical behaviour along the series?
cards.definition: Early members reactive like calcium; later ones more like aluminium

cards.term: E°(Ln³⁺/Ln) range?
cards.definition: −2.2 to −2.4 V (Eu −2.0 V)

cards.term: Carbides formed by lanthanoids?
cards.definition: Ln₃C, Ln₂C₃, LnC₂ on heating with carbon

cards.term: Nature of Ln(OH)₃?
cards.definition: Definite compounds (not hydrated oxides), basic like alkaline earth hydroxides

cards.term: Figure 4.7 · Chemical reactions of the lanthanoids
Best single use of lanthanoids?
cards.definition: Alloy steels for plates and pipes

cards.term: Composition and use of mischmetall?
cards.definition: ~95% lanthanoid + ~5% Fe + traces of S, C, Ca, Al; in Mg alloys for bullets, shells, lighter flints

cards.term: Other uses of lanthanoid oxides?
cards.definition: Mixed oxides: catalysts in petroleum cracking; some as phosphors in TV screens

cards.term: Actinoid half-lives?
cards.definition: Early members long later ones from a day down to 3 min (Lr) latter made only in nanogram amounts

cards.term: General configuration of actinoids?
cards.definition: 7s² with variable 5f and 6d occupancy

cards.term: Configurations of Am and Cm?
cards.definition: Am [Rn]5f⁷7s²; Cm [Rn]5f⁷6d¹7s²

cards.term: Why do 5f electrons bond more than 4f?
cards.definition: 5f orbitals are less buried (less shielded inside the core)

cards.term: Why is actinoid contraction greater per element than lanthanoid? (Intext 4.10)
cards.definition: Poorer shielding by 5f electrons

cards.term: Why do actinoids show many oxidation states?
cards.definition: 5f, 6d and 7s levels have comparable energies

cards.term: Maximum oxidation states of Th, Pa, U, Np?
cards.definition: +4, +5, +6, +7; then decrease

cards.term: Common oxidation state of actinoids?
cards.definition: +3 (more compounds in +3 than +4); +3 and +4 ions tend to hydrolyse

cards.term: Actinoid metals: appearance and structures?
cards.definition: All silvery; variety of structures (irregular metallic radii)

cards.term: Reactions of actinoids with water, HCl, HNO₃, alkali?
cards.definition: Boiling water: oxide + hydride. HCl attacks all. HNO₃: slight (protective oxide). Alkalis: no action.

cards.term: Actinoid vs lanthanoid magnetic behaviour?
cards.definition: Actinoids more complex; lanthanoids have higher susceptibility values

cards.term: Why are IEs of early actinoids lower than early lanthanoids?
cards.definition: 5f penetrates less, is more shielded, so outer electrons are held less firmly

cards.term: Why is lanthanoid contraction more important than actinoid contraction?
cards.definition: Chemistry of elements after actinoids is much less known

cards.term: Metals added to steel?
cards.definition: Cr, Mn, Ni (plus carbon)

cards.term: Correction: NCERT says "TiO for the pigment industry." Actual pigment?
cards.definition: TiO₂ (titanium dioxide, white pigment)

cards.term: MnO₂ and Zn, Ni/Cd used in?
cards.definition: Battery industry (MnO₂ in dry cells)

cards.term: Why are group 11 elements called coinage metals? Modern UK coins?
cards.definition: Cu, Ag, Au; UK "copper" coins are copper-coated steel, "silver" coins Cu/Ni alloy

cards.text:
Catalysts: {{c1::V₂O₅}} oxidises SO₂ (H₂SO₄)
{{c2::TiCl₄ + Al(CH₃)₃}} = Ziegler catalyst (polythene)
{{c3::Fe}} in Haber process
{{c4::Ni}} hydrogenates fats.

cards.term: NCERT: Wacker process oxidises ethyne to ethanal with PdCl₂. Correction?
cards.definition: Wacker process oxidises ethene (ethylene) to ethanal: CH₂=CH₂ + ½O₂ → CH₃CHO (PdCl₂/CuCl₂)

cards.term: Uses of Ni complexes and AgBr?
cards.definition: Ni complexes: polymerisation of alkynes, benzene formation. AgBr: photography (light-sensitive).

cards.term: Lanthanoids vs actinoids
cards.definition: Orbitals filled: 4f  |  5f; Common state: +3  |  +3, many higher (to +7); Radioactivity: Only Pm  |  All; Contraction per element: Smaller  |  Larger (poorer 5f shielding); f electrons in bonding: Buried, little  |  More involved
